rules.rationale: Many N/O heteroatoms enable hydrogen bonding with water, the dominant favorable term in hydration free energy.
Heavy halogenation gives low-polarity, hydrophobic surfaces with poor water hydrogen bonding and high cavity cost.
Moderate polarity without halogens is the classic hydrophilic small-solute regime in aqueous solvation datasets.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the low-confidence ESOL size prior, since longer polar chains can add hydrating functional groups.

skill.hypothesis: Assumes hydration affinity tracks polar hydrogen-bonding capacity and penalizes halogenated hydrophobes, downweighting the uncertain ESOL size prior. Fails if the score instead rewards small nonpolar solutes.

hypothesis_snapshot.evidence_boundary: Finite-pool LLM-direct baseline: rule weights remain frozen and are not calibrated from target observations. Target observations only update the shared GP-UCB/EI anchor.
